title: Erdős-Hajnal Conjecture (Conjecture 1.1)
statement_text: For every graph $H$, there exists $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\max(\alpha(G), \omega(G)) \geq |V(G)|^{\varepsilon}$.
context_text: The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture [5, 6] is confirmed for all $H$ with at most four vertices but remains open for $H = C_5$. The case $H = C_5$ is particularly notable because $C_5$ is self-complementary, so excluding $C_5$ simultaneously excludes its complement, an approach that has been fruitful in related work.
paper_contribution: Proves that for every $C_5$-free graph $G$ with $n > 1$ vertices, $\max(\alpha(G), \omega(G)) \geq 2^{c\sqrt{\log n \log \log n}}$, improving the previously best known general bound of $2^{c\sqrt{\log n}}$ when $H = C_5$.
paper_title: Towards Erdos-Hajnal for graphs with no 5-hole

title: Conlon-Fox-Sudakov Conjecture (Conjecture 1.4)
statement_text: For every graph $H$ there exist $\varepsilon, \sigma > 0$ such that for every $H$-free graph $G$ on $n > 1$ vertices, and all $c$ with $0 \leq c \leq 1/2$, $V(G)$ contains two disjoint subsets $A, B$ with $|A| \geq \varepsilon c^{\sigma} n$ and $|B| \geq \varepsilon n$, such that the edge-density between $A, B$ is either at most $c$ or at least $1 - c$.
context_text: Conjecture 1.4, due to Conlon, Fox and Sudakov [4, problem 3.13], generalises a bipartite density-separation property for $H$-free graphs and had not been proved for any graph $H$ with more than four vertices prior to this paper. Proving it for $H = C_5$ is the key step in establishing the improved Erdős-Hajnal bound 1.3.
paper_contribution: Proves Conjecture 1.4 for $H = C_5$ with $\sigma = 1$, via a direct argument for sparse graphs combined with Rödl's theorem to handle the general case.
paper_title: Towards Erdos-Hajnal for graphs with no 5-hole

title: Polynomial dependence of $\delta$ on $d$ in Rödl's theorem
statement_text: A polynomial dependence of $\delta$ on $d$ holds in Rödl's theorem (for every graph $H$ and all $d>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that for every $H$-free graph $G$ there exists $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $|X|\ge\delta|V(G)|$ such that in one of $G[X]$, $\overline{G}[X]$ every vertex of $X$ has degree at most $d|X|$), i.e., the $\delta$ satisfying Rödl's theorem can be taken to be polynomial in $d$; and this would imply the Erdős-Hajnal conjecture itself.
context_text: Here $H$-free means with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$, $\alpha(G)$ and $\omega(G)$ are the stability and clique numbers, $\overline{G}$ is the complement of $G$, and logarithms are base $2$. The Erdős–Hajnal conjecture asserts that for every graph $H$ there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that every $H$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\max(\alpha(G),\omega(G))\ge|V(G)|^\varepsilon$; the best general bound, due to Erdős and Hajnal, is $2^{c\sqrt{\log n}}$. From $d,\delta$ satisfying Rödl's theorem one gets, by Turán's theorem, a stable set or clique of size about $\min(\frac{1}{2d},\frac{\delta n}{2})$, so better bounds in Rödl's theorem give better Erdős–Hajnal-type bounds. Rödl's original proof uses the regularity lemma and gives a tower-type bound on $1/\delta$; Fox and Sudakov proved $\delta=2^{-15|V(H)|(\log(1/d))^2}$, which implies the Erdős–Hajnal bound $2^{c\sqrt{\log n}}$. The statement that a polynomial dependence holds (presumably $\delta=d^{C}$ for some constant $C$ depending on $H$) is presented as a known conjecture without attribution. For $H=C_5$ the authors indicate that one can take $\delta=2^{-O((\log(1/d))^2/\log\log(1/d))}$, giving another route to their main result $\max(\alpha(G),\omega(G))\ge2^{c\sqrt{\log n\log\log n}}$ for $C_5$-free graphs.
notes: Stated in passive voice ('It is conjectured that…') without a specific citation; appears to be a community/folklore conjecture presented without explicit attribution. For $H = C_5$ the authors note one can achieve the intermediate bound $\delta = 2^{-O((\log(1/d))^2 / \log\log(1/d))}$.
paper_title: Towards Erdos-Hajnal for graphs with no 5-hole
